newsitem.title: INDIA: Gujral says Kashmir always to remain part of India.
newsitem.headline: Gujral says Kashmir always to remain part of India.

text.p: Indian Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral on Thursday said India and Pakistan were eager to improve frosty ties but New Delhi would always view the divided Himalayan region of Kashmir as an integral part of India.
"To defend the secular tradition of our country, if anyone tries to cause harm to it from inside or outside, is our primary duty," Gujral said in an interview broadcast on state-run television.
"Kashmir is an integral part of India and will always remain so," he said.
India controls two thirds of Kashmir and neighbouring Pakistan the rest. The two nations have fought two wars over the region since independence from British colonial rule in 1947.
India has repeatedly accused Pakistan of training and arming separatist rebels in the Moslem-majority region -- a charge Islamabad denies.
Police and hospitals say more than 20,000 people have died since the insurgency erupted in 1990 in Kashmir, where guerrillas are fighting for either independence or merger with Pakistan.
Gujral said: "In recent days, it looks like both of us now understand that we both end up losing because of the kind of relations we have shared."
Gujral and Pakistani Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif held talks earlier this month at a regional summit in the Maldives -- the first talks between the archrivals' leaders in four years.
The top diplomats from both countries met in March after a gap of three years, and are due to meet in Islamabad next month.
Pakistan says Kashmir is the core issue in bilateral talks. India says it is keen to make headway in discussions on trade and other less contentious matters.

After the talks in the Maldives, India said it planned to start buying electricity from its neighbour, perhaps as early as next year. The two countries also agreed to free all of each other's civilian prisoners and to set up a direct hotline between Gujral and Sharif.
